subject: DONE s337c (6c5ece9): shared announce/die helpers + audit of pcl-runtime.lisp — 38 sites, no value-producing swallow left
description:
DONE s337c, commit 6c5ece9.  Gate 131/4594 PASS.

STEP 1 (as ruled, done first): ONE shared pair of helpers with ONE dedup table — %p-announce-unsupported (site operand) for EFFECT-ONLY, %p-unsupported-value (site operand) for VALUE-PRODUCING.  The per-site hash s337 had just added for SvREADONLY was folded into it and its three call sites migrated to (site, operand) pairs.

AUDIT of cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: every (t …)/(otherwise …) arm whose body is a bare nil/0/""/*p-undef*/t = 38 sites (inventory script + context dump in scratchpad rule12-sites.txt).  Result:
- ~33 are PERL'S OWN TOTAL RULES, not swallowed cases: %p-true-p-slow (everything not explicitly false is true), %to-number-raw (anything else is 0), p-ref (non-reference is ""), p-wantarray (third arm), p-aref/p-shift (past-the-end is undef, with %p-wrong-referent-p dying AHEAD of them), sprintf's prefix/sign conds (no flag applies), p--T/p--B (closed scan result), p-glob-slot (already carries an explicit "this IS the Perl semantics" comment), p-get-class/%p-target-class/%pcl-invocant-class (no class), p-chop-one/p-chomp-one (non-modifiable = principle 9).
- THE ARCHETYPE IS ALREADY FIXED: p-vec's width dispatch handles 16/32/64 in one loop and DIES on an illegal width; its surviving (t 0) is only sub-byte-access-past-the-end, which is correct perl.
- ONE family had a real smell — see below.

THE ONE FINDING, and why both fixes were REVERTED (measurements recorded in %p-out-fh-or-fail so they are not retried):
print/printf/say each carried their OWN COPY of "unresolvable handle → EBADF, write nothing, return false, say nothing".  Three copies → one %p-out-fh-or-fail (CLAUDE.md 11).  That part shipped.  But:
 (a) WARN "print() on unopened filehandle NAME"?  NO — use-warnings-GATED in perl, not default-on.  Measured (scratchpad w1.pl vs w2.pl): plain perl prints nothing and returns undef, exactly like PCL.  Emitting it unconditionally broke Pl/t/fileio-02.t and Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t, which assert the default quiet.  PCL tracks NO warnings state anywhere (grepped Pl/ and cl/).
 (b) DIE "Can't use an undefined value as a symbol reference"?  Right for a handle NEVER OPENED, but perl returns undef for a CLOSED one — and PCL cannot tell them apart because %p-forget-fh leaves the variable UNDEFINED after close.  Dying broke transpile-test-09.t's closed-handle rows (#186), which are right.

OPEN, handed to Fable in docs/opus5-review-requests-s337.md §3-§4:
 1. SCOPE — only cl/pcl-runtime.lisp was audited.  cl/pcl-test.lisp was #202's subject; cl/pcl-xs.lisp unaudited; pcl-pack.lisp/pcl-mro.lisp are generated (auditing them = auditing cl/pack-impl.pl and lib/mro.pm).
 2. NET — the grep catches only CONSTANT default bodies; a default arm that CALLS something is missed.  Widening = reading every cond tail in 16k lines; worth a session given result (1)?
 3. Is a CLOSED-HANDLE VALUE (something close() leaves behind that is defined-but-not-writable) worth its own task?  It would buy the undef-designator die.  Suggested: queue behind #153/E4.1.
 4. Smaller: p-getprotobyname answers from a FOUR-ENTRY static table and returns undef for anything else, where perl reads /etc/protocols.
